suggestions: Replace the single 10-day volume confirmation with a dual-horizon co-movement blend, e.g., average Corr(Ma((close-low)/(high-low),5), Log(Ma(volume,5)/Ma(volume,40)), 20) and Corr(same range leg, same volume trend, 60), then Rank over 20 days before combining. Investment rationale: short-window price–volume correlation is highly regime-sensitive and often inverts during liquidity shocks; blending medium- and long-horizon alignment keeps the participation leg directionally consistent, reducing year-to-year RankIC sign flips that depress RankIR.

Restructure the composite from multiplicative rank interaction to an additive rank consensus with stronger temporal persistence: Ma((Rank(Zscore(Ma((close-low)/(high-low),5),20),20) + Rank(dual-horizon Corr leg, 20)) / 2, 8). Investment rationale: multiplying ranks forces both legs to be simultaneously extreme, so a temporary dip in either leg collapses the score and reshuffles cross-sectional ordering; averaging ranks preserves partial conviction when one signal softens, and a longer final smoother damps day-to-day rank churn that drives high turnover and unstable out-of-sample RankIR.

Stabilize the range-strength leg with a volatility-regime normalizer before ranking: divide the smoothed range-position series by Ma(Std(Ma((close-low)/(high-low),5), 20), 20), then apply Zscore/Rank. Investment rationale: raw close-in-range readings are inflated in tight, low-information bars and compressed in wide-range regimes; scaling by recent range-position variability down-weights noise-driven highs and makes the strength signal comparable across volatility cycles, improving temporal consistency of predictive rank ordering.
